acceptanceCriteria: Define closed admitted per-run Gradle user-home/cache and daemon ownership semantics before launching new qualification; retain library provenance and supported commands.

Run actual native Gradle test body/helper readiness and timeout/interruption through current common executor with fixed expected native IDs and pinned tools/source/config; qualify or retain exact owned survivors and limits.
Preserve historical plans/receipts and ambient daemons, require bounded failure/cancellation cleanup and independent source/CEM/native completion evidence or true integration blocker.
body: Observed qualification precondition gap, not a confirmed cleanup failure. Owner CEM1.0 all-main-runner scope. Existing Gradle9.6.1 common-profile native transcript explicitly forks a single-use Daemon despite --no-daemon. Current fixed Invocation has no independently admitted per-run Gradle user-home/start/socket identity; shared user caches/ambient daemons must be preserved. Native qualifier therefore did not launch new Gradle timeout/interrupt test; classification NOT_RUN_OWNERSHIP_PRECONDITION, actual /private/tmp/cem10-build/stable-next/jvm-lifecycle/qualification.json SHA5f1bf725072506ee8dd8d1578ad4baa94e2342055fc4023c536942cb2236746f plus native-platform-plan rowjvm-build-launchers. Installed Core1.0.0-rc.1build163/Tasksbuild202; clean05d source treeequals163b. Expected safe fixed optional profile admits confined isolated home and scoped daemon identity before launch, records lifecycle uncertainty, preserves shared caches/devices/processes. No broad gradle --stop, killall, raceable snapshot-as-proof or original historical-byte rewrite.
title: Gradle lifecycle qualification needs admitted isolated single-use daemon ownership
